gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured idle draw, efficiency or surge figure from a named reviewer or lab for any 24 V split-phase inverter, and I could not source one either, so this angle adds nothing new that can go on the page.
standout_why: I compared against these rival pages: the cited Sigineer APC6024D page, liveoffthegrid.com/specs/inverters and off-grid-benchmark.pages.dev. The Sigineer page already gives its own rated figures: 80 W idle, 15 W in power saver, 88% peak efficiency and 3,000 W per 120 V leg. liveoffthegrid lists no 24 V split-phase units at all; its table has only 48 V split-phase units, with figures copied from datasheets and no tester named. off-grid-benchmark says its rankings come from a 'spec-based scorecard'. None of these pages has a named measurement. But I found nothing I could open that has one either. The only figures I could source are maker ratings, and the cited rival already has those for the Sigineer.
decides: This doesn't change the pick. No named reviewer has published a bench test of the 24 V split-phase candidates (Sigineer APC6024D, SunGold Power LFP6K24V240VSP, AIMS PICOGLF60W24V240VS / 4000 W 24 V, WZRELB 4000 W 24 V) that I could open, so measurements can't separate them. The maker ratings do point to one practical difference. Sigineer rates its 6,000 W unit at 80 W idle, which is about 1.9 kWh a day if left on. AIMS rates its 4,000 W 24 V unit at 52.5 W idle. Each maker's power-saver mode is rated well below those numbers. So for small, constant loads, idle draw and power-saver behavior matter more than the headline wattage. Those are the makers' claims, not test results.

findings.label: Rated idle draw (maker spec, not a measurement)
findings.value: 80 W idle; 15 W in power saver mode
findings.source_title: 6000 Watt Inverter 24Vdc to 120V 240Vac Split Phase Pure Sine Wave – With 85A Battery Charger – Sigineer Power
findings.note: This is the maker's rating. The page has no test data. 80 W × 24 h = 1.92 kWh a day with no load.

findings.label: Rated per-leg output and efficiency (maker spec)
findings.value: 3,000 W per 120 V leg (6,000 W only at 240 V); 88% peak DC-to-AC efficiency; 18,000 W surge for 20 s
findings.source_title: 6000 Watt Inverter 24Vdc to 120V 240Vac Split Phase Pure Sine Wave – With 85A Battery Charger – Sigineer Power
findings.note: This is ChatGPT's cited page, so the rival already has these figures. The page listed a price of $949.00 (was $1,199.00) on the day I read it.

findings.label: Rated idle draw (maker spec, not a measurement)
findings.value: 52.5 W idle; under 25 W with power saver on
findings.source_title: 4000 Watt Pure Sine Inverter Charger 24Vdc to 120/240Vac Split Phase - AIMS Power
findings.note: AIMS's Canadian store, which is result 17. It also lists 12,000 W surge for 20 s, more than 88% peak efficiency and UL 458 / UL 1741 / CSA 22.2 listings. The price shown is in CAD and the page says it needs a custom quote, so I'm not using it as a US price.

unsourced: A named reviewer or lab measurement (Will Prowse, The Solar Lab, Hobotech, a magazine lab) of idle draw, efficiency or surge for any 24 V split-phase inverter. Searches turned up 48 V split-phase reviews only (The Solar Lab: EG4 6000XP, WattCycle 6kW, EG4 12000XP).
